title: Auto Loans: Prepayment Charge in a Payoff
content:
Closing an Auto Loans account early with money moved from the borrower's own PCB checking can carry a charge for repaying ahead of schedule, depending on the product's prepayment rate. This note states when that charge is added and how it is sized.

## Rule

- When the product's prepayment rate is above zero, a prepayment charge is added to the payoff: that rate, as a percentage, of the capital balance, rounded to the cent.
- When the product's prepayment rate is zero, nothing is added.

## Condition, judgement, outcome

| Product's prepayment rate | Charge added to the payoff |
|---|---|
| above zero | the rate's percentage of the capital balance, to the cent |
| zero | none |

## Illustration (invented rate)

Were a product's prepayment rate 1.00 percent, a capital balance of 12389.45 would bring a charge of 123.89. With a rate of zero, the same balance brings no charge at all.
